facts.statement: The technology is called Electrochemical Magnetic Induction Spectroscopy (EMIS) and is described as agnostic to cell chemistry, size and shape.
facts.quote: EMIS is chemistry, size & shape agnostic.

facts.statement: In its present form the output is a 2D image showing where the abnormality is and how severe it is.
facts.quote: a 2D imaging showing the location of the abnormality inside the cell, along with a measure of its severity

facts.statement: The Phase IIB goal is to turn the output into one or two numbers so a machine can read it.
facts.quote: The EMIS output will be a scalar quantity (such as one or two numbers)

facts.statement: The plan says the product is designed to be integrated into customers' existing ACIR testing machines.
facts.quote: we have designed EMIS to be integrated into customers’ existing ACIR testing machines

facts.statement: The only hardware added to an ACIR station is said to be a thin sensor plate above the cell.
facts.quote: The only added hardware is a thin (less than 1mm thick) plate at a fixed distance above the battery surface

facts.statement: The quality-control version of the product is named the PES scanner.
facts.quote: PES scanner is the name of EMIS for Q.C. applications.

facts.statement: The proposal describes the prospective product as an autonomous cell testing machine for ACIR stations, or alternatively a benchtop machine for research labs.
facts.quote: An autonomous cell testing machine that can be integrated to ACIR stations at manufacturing lines.
facts.date_of_claim: 2024 (proposal itself undated; companion plan dated April 2024)
facts.notes: Next sentence in source: 'Alternatively it can be a benchtop machine similar to EIS machines for research labs.'

facts.statement: The system is described as a magnetometer array about 1 cm above the cell, a signal generator and a data acquisition system feeding a Python program.
facts.quote: an array of magnetometers about 1 cm above the surface of the battery, a signal generator sending an AC signal
facts.date_of_claim: 2024 (proposal itself undated; companion plan dated April 2024)

facts.statement: The proposal states the method works from 20 mAh to 100 Ah cells and without electrolyte.
facts.quote: EMIS is agnostic to size (from 20 mAh to 100 Ah cells), shape and chemistry, and works even in the absence of electrolyte.
facts.date_of_claim: 2024 (proposal itself undated; companion plan dated April 2024)

facts.statement: The September 2025 deck names the first product EMIS-B, a benchtop version for research labs.
facts.quote: First product: EMIS-B, Benchtop version for Research labs

facts.statement: The deck says the impedance (EIS) function and the magnetic mapping share the same electronics.
facts.quote: Electronics: EIS and EMIS share same electronics

facts.statement: The deck states an achieved impedance specification of 0.005 mOhm maximum error over six hours.
facts.quote: Impedance: maximum error of 0.005 mOhm over 6 hours of testing

facts.statement: The deck claims in-house electronics accuracy better than 0.005 mOhm at 2.5 mOhm and calls this ten times better than a Gamry instrument.
facts.quote: Demonstrated better than 0.005 mOhm accuracy at 2.5 mOhm using our inhouse electronics (at 0.02%, it is 10X better than Gamry at 0.2%)
facts.notes: Arithmetic check on the document's own numbers: 0.005 / 2.5 = 0.2%, not 0.02%. See contradictions.

facts.statement: The deck calls the manufacturer quality-control use the second product.
facts.quote: EMIS value for manufacturers: Our second product

facts.quote: No linear stage, 10mm resolution Find defective cells Output: Good vs. Bad (threshold)

contradictions.detail: Hardware cost history differs. The April 2024 plan (and the positioning document) say $50k, then $4k, then $1k. The September 2025 deck says $100,000, then $10,000, then $2,000.
Within the same deck, slide 2 says Phase IIB year 1 reached $2,000 while the March 2025 slide says Phase IIB reached $1,000. The plan had already claimed $1k from Phase II in April 2024.
Sensor cost. The plan stresses phone magnetometer chips at $0.10 to $0.20 each; the deck lists the magnetometers actually purchased at $100 to $1000 per channel.
The same plan gives two chip prices: less than $0.20 on page 7 and about $0.10 on page 8.
Patent counts vary: nearly 52 (plan page 12), more than 9 directly related (plan page 13), over 45 originated by the team (proposal page 18). The scopes may differ but are not reconciled.
Nearly 52 issued and pending patents versus over 45 patents originated by the team.
Caltech's spend on patent protection is given as about $1.5M (all patents) and about $500,000 (patents directly related to this technology). Possibly different scopes; not reconciled.
The same patent title appears with two different numbers: 9658292 in the proposal and 10955483 in the plan. The relation (for example a continuation) is not explained.
The plan says two provisional patents were filed; the proposal mentions one.
Headcount: two full-time employees plus three part-time consultants (plan) versus a four-person spinoff growing to five (proposal).
The proposal lists three subcontractors including NREL; the September 2025 deck lists only LG Energy Solution and LBNL. NREL's status is not explained.
The same plan says manufacturing quality control is the main business focus and also that the first product is focused on research labs.
The plan says the company chose not to sell hardware and that customers will build it; the product sheet offers the hardware for rental at a stated price.
The plan says the company decided against selling hardware products; the positioning document says the company sells the instrument now.
The proposal says machine-readable output would be finished before shipping to customers; the positioning document says the 2D-map instrument is sold now.
The plan promises about a dozen prototypes; the proposal promises 10 units.
Internal arithmetic: 0.005 mOhm at 2.5 mOhm is 0.2%, but the deck states 0.02% and uses that to claim ten times better than Gamry at 0.2%.
Accuracy levels differ by document: the product sheet states 0.3% for local resistance variation; the engineering agreement's acceptance test only requires ACIR within 5% of a reference.
The product sheet gives 10 Hz to 10 kHz in the highlights and 100 Hz to 10 kHz in the mode description.
Current range: the product sheet and agreement milestone 2 give up to 1000 mA; the agreement's page 4 requirements give 10 mA to 5 A (and a 50 A pulse).
Inside the agreement, milestone 2 specifies three ranges up to 1000 mA while the page 4 requirements specify 10 mA to 5 A.
Channel count: the product sheet model has 8 mapper channels; the engineering agreement's final milestone is a 64-channel board; the audit saw two eight-channel modules.
The agreement's final milestone is a 64-channel board; the November 2026 audit describes two eight-channel modules before board integration.
Sample rate wording: the agreement says 50 kHz ADC, the deck says 64 kS/s, the audit reports 62.5 kS/s per channel.
Gantry repeatability: plus or minus 50 micrometres on the product sheet versus better than 0.025 mm in the agreement; the deck gives 0.050 mm accuracy.
Payment timing inside the agreement: 15 days after verification in clause 2.1, 30 days after verification in each milestone.
Clause 2.1 makes the contractor responsible for hiring subcontractors; clause 14.1 forbids subcontracting without written consent.
Milestones were due 20 August 2024 and the agreement ended 31 March 2025; an audit dated 17 November 2026 says completion against the agreed requirements is still not established.

The proposal says the electrical engineering consultant is compensated from overhead if and when needed; the agreement with the same person carries a fee of up to $145,000 on a government-funded project.
The 30 Ah Farasis cells are called NMC on slide 4 and LFP on slides 18 and 19.
Torn-tab cells are 59 Ah in the plan and proposal and 60 Ah in the deck.
The roadmap marks internal short circuit detection as validated with NREL's device; the proposal only proposes that work, and the deck attributes short-circuit cells to Idaho National Lab.
Roadmap says tested with NREL's device; deck says the cells came from Idaho National Lab.
The roadmap's key message is 'first and only'; the positioning document says not to claim 'only' because other serious players exist.
The plan says the company is the first and only group with freedom to operate; the positioning document acknowledges other serious players in magnetic current-density imaging.
The plan calls the product an extra tool; the positioning document says that framing must be dropped.
Cell size range: 20 mAh to 100 Ah as a general claim, 200 mAh to 100 Ah in the work plan.
The equity plan section says the company is focused on developing advanced batteries for power tools and vehicles, which does not match the sensing instrument the rest of the proposal describes.
Entity naming: the grant and agreement use Parthian Energy LLC; one deck slide is marked Parthian Technologies; the product sheet uses only 'PNRG'.
Two unrelated pricing models appear with no bridge between them: $1 per scanned kWh for software (plan) and a fixed rental of the instrument (product sheet).
The deck reports the year-one go decision as passed while saying the core choice of analysis method was still undecided.
